extracted.intended_audience: federal agency NEPA practitioners, agency counsel, environmental review staff, and applicants preparing or overseeing EAs/EISs
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards for Federal agencies to prepare, adopt, file, and manage NEPA environmental documents (EAs, EISs, categorical exclusions), supervise contractor/applicant-prepared materials, coordinate with other jurisdictions, and ensure scientific integrity and public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim major Federal actions during environmental review
rubrics_metrics.description: While work on a required environmental review for a program is in progress and an action is not covered by an existing environmental document, agencies shall not undertake in the interim any major Federal action that may significantly affect the quality of the human environment unless such action:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Is justified independently of the program; (2) Is itself accompanied by an adequate environmental review; and (3) Will not prejudice the ultimate decision on the program. Interim action prejudices the ultimate decision when it tends to determine subsequent development or limit alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation to eliminate duplication with State, Tribal, and local procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: To the fullest extent practicable unless specifically prohibited by law, agencies shall cooperate with State, Tribal, and local agencies responsible for preparing environmental documents to reduce duplication between NEPA and State/Tribal/local requirements, including through use of studies, analyses, and decisions developed by those agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation should include joint planning processes; joint environmental research and studies; joint public hearings (except where statute provides otherwise); joint environmental assessments; and, where practicable, joint environmental impact statements with joint lead agencies. Where additional non-conflicting State/Tribal/local requirements exist, agencies may cooperate so one document will comply with all applicable laws. Environmental impact statements should discuss any inconsistency with approved State/Tribal/local plans and describe the extent to which reconciliation would occur (NEPA does not require reconciliation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of other agencies' environmental documents
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt another agency's draft or final environmental impact statement, environmental assessment, or categorical exclusion determination provided the adopting agency conducts an independent review and concludes the statement/assessment meets the standards for adequacy under this subchapter and the adopting agency's procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If actions covered are substantially the same, the adopting agency shall republish and file the EIS as a final statement consistent with §1506.9. If not substantially the same or supplementation is required, treat as draft/supplement and republish. Cooperating agencies may issue a ROD adopting a lead agency EIS without republication in some circumstances. For EAs, adoption allowed when actions are substantially the same and EA meets adequacy standards; otherwise adopt and supplement or reevaluate and issue a FONSI with notice. For categorical exclusion determinations, the adopting agency must document adoption (showing substantial sameness and absence of extraordinary circumstances) and publish the adoption determination on an agency website or otherwise make it publicly available. The adopting agency must specify if the adopted document is not final within the original agency, is the subject of a referral under part 1504, or is subject to unresolved judicial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining environmental documents with other agency documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should combine, to the fullest extent practicable, any environmental document with any other agency document to reduce duplication and paperwork.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining documents is encouraged where consistent with statutory requirements to facilitate efficient decisionmaking and avoid redundant materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibility for accuracy, scope, content, and professional integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency is responsible for the accuracy, scope, and content of environmental documents and shall ensure they are prepared with professional and scientific integrity, using reliable data and resources, regardless of whether prepared by agency staff, contractors, or applicants under agency procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency shall exercise independent judgment and briefly document its determination that an environmental document meets NEPA standards, the regulations in this subchapter, and the agency's NEPA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of applicant-provided information
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may require an applicant to submit environmental information for possible use by the agency in preparing an environmental document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency should assist applicants by outlining the types of information required. The agency shall independently evaluate any information submitted by an applicant and, to the extent it is integrated into the environmental document, be responsible for its accuracy, scope, and contents. Agencies may allow applicants to prepare EAs and EISs pursuant to agency procedures consistent with section 107(f) of NEPA, but such procedures must meet agency oversight standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-directed contractor preparation and oversight of environmental documents
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may authorize a contractor to prepare an environmental document under the supervision and direction of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must provide guidance and participate in and supervise the contractor's preparation; independently evaluate contractor-prepared documents and document that evaluation in the environmental document; include names and qualifications of persons preparing and evaluating the documents (e.g., list of preparers for EISs); and prepare a disclosure statement for the contractor declaring no financial or other interest in the outcome (excluding trade secrets/confidential business info). The intent is to verify acceptable work, not to redo it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and scientific accuracy standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall ensure the professional integrity, including scientific integrity, of discussions and analyses in environmental documents and use high-quality information, including reliable data, resources, models, and Indigenous Knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may rely on existing information and on new information obtained for analysis, including remotely gathered data or statistical models. Agencies shall explain relevant assumptions or limitations of information or models, identify methodologies used, and explicitly reference scientific and other sources relied upon for conclusions (methodology discussion may be placed in an appendix). Where appropriate, agencies shall use projections (including for climate change-related effects) and disclose assumptions or limitations for models that project ranges of possible future outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA integration for proposals for legislation and legislative EISs
rubrics_metrics.description: When developing legislation, agencies shall integrate the NEPA process for proposals significantly affecting the human environment with Congress's legislative process. A legislative EIS is the detailed statement required by law to be included in an agency's recommendation or report on a legislative proposal to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical drafting assistance alone is not a legislative proposal. Only the agency with primary responsibility for the subject prepares a legislative EIS. The legislative EIS may be transmitted up to 30 days after the recommendation to allow accurate completion; it must be available in time for Congressional hearings and deliberations. Preparation shall conform to this subchapter except scoping need not be done; agencies prepare legislative statements like draft EISs and need not prepare final statements unless specified conditions exist (e.g., Congressional committee rules, statutorily required study process, site-specific project location, or agency decision). Comments on the legislative statement go to the lead agency which forwards them and responses to Congressional committees with jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing environmental impact statements with EPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall file environmental impact statements together with comments and responses with the Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Federal Activities, consistent with EPA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must file statements with EPA no earlier than when they are also transmitted to participating agencies and made available to the public. EPA may issue guidelines to implement its responsibilities and agencies shall file adoptions of EISs with EPA (see §1506.3(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing rules for records of decision and comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies shall not make or issue a record of decision (ROD) for a proposed action until the later of: (1) 90 days after publication of EPA's weekly notice for a draft EIS; or (2) 30 days after publication of EPA's weekly notice for a final EIS, unless otherwise provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (a) Where formal administrative review processes (appeals/objections/protests) provide a real opportunity to alter the decision, decision and the 30-day period may run concurrently if explained in the EIS; (b) Agencies engaged in rulemaking to protect public health or safety may waive the 30-day period and publish the decision simultaneously, with notice. If a final EIS is filed within 90 days of the draft filing, 30-day and 90-day periods may run concurrently, but agencies shall allow at least 45 days for comments on draft statements. The lead agency may extend minimum periods and must notify consistent with §1506.9. EPA may reduce or extend periods for compelling national policy reasons; the lead agency may modify periods to comply with other statutory requirements. Failure to file timely comments is not sufficient reason to extend a period. If the lead agency does not concur in an extension, EPA may not extend more than 30 days and must notify the Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency NEPA compliance arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where emergency circumstances make it necessary to take action with significant effects without observing the regulations, the Federal agency taking the action shall consult with the Council about alternative arrangements for compliance with NEPA section 102(2)(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies and the Council shall limit arrangements to actions necessary to control immediate impacts of the emergency; other actions remain subject to normal NEPA review. Alternative arrangements do not waive the statutory requirement to comply with NEPA, but establish alternate means for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory agency compliance with the NEPA subchapter
rubrics_metrics.description: All agencies of the Federal Government shall comply with the regulations in this subchapter, with the intent to allow each agency flexibility in adapting implementing procedures authorized by §1507.3 to other applicable laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of senior NEPA official and Chief Public Engagement Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall designate a senior agency official responsible for overall review of agency NEPA compliance (resolving implementation issues) and a Chief Public Engagement Officer responsible for facilitating community engagement in environmental reviews and, where appropriate, provision of technical assistance to communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For departments, major subunits may identify senior officials or Officers within subunits with consent of the department-level official, whom the department-level official or Officer oversees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of a systematic, interdisciplinary approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall fulfill section 102(2)(A) of NEPA to utilize a systematic, interdisciplinary approach ensuring integrated use of natural and social sciences and environmental design arts in planning and decisionmaking that may impact the human environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of methods to consider unquantified environmental amenities and values
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall identify methods and procedures required by section 102(2)(B) of NEPA to ensure presently unquantified environmental amenities and values may be given appropriate consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of adequate environmental impact statements and cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall prepare adequate environmental impact statements pursuant to section 102(2)(C) of NEPA and cooperate on the development of EISs in areas where the agency has jurisdiction by law or special expertise or is authorized to develop and enforce environmental standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure environmental documents are prepared with professional integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall ensure environmental documents are prepared with professional integrity, including scientific integrity, consistent with section 102(2)(D) of NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reliable data and resources in NEPA work
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall make use of reliable data and resources in carrying out NEPA responsibilities, consistent with section 102(2)(E) of NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study, develop, and describe technically and economically feasible alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall study, develop, and describe technically and economically feasible alternatives consistent with section 102(2)(F) of NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study alternatives for unresolved conflicts over resource uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall study, develop, and describe alternatives to recommended courses of action in any proposal that involves unresolved conflicts concerning alternative uses of available resources, consistent with section 102(2)(H) of NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate and utilize ecological information in planning resource-oriented projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall comply with the requirement of section 102(2)(K) of NEPA that the agency initiate and utilize ecological information in the planning and development of resource-oriented projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fulfill requirements of other NEPA sections and relevant Executive Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall fulfill the requirements of sections 102(2)(I), 102(2)(J), and 102(2)(L) of NEPA, and Executive Order 11514 (as amended), relating to protection and enhancement of environmental quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and consultation for developing or revising agency NEPA procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than 12 months after July 1, 2024 (or 9 months after establishment of an agency), each agency shall develop or revise proposed procedures to implement these regulations, facilitate efficient decisionmaking, and ensure decisions accord with NEPA policies and requirements. Agencies shall consult with the Council while developing procedures and before publishing them in the Federal Register for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies with similar programs should consult with each other and the Council to coordinate procedures. Agencies shall provide an opportunity for public review and Council review for conformity before issuing final procedures; the Council shall complete review within 30 days of receipt of proposed final procedures. Once in effect, agencies shall publish their NEPA procedures and ensure they are readily available to the public, and continue to review and revise as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency NEPA procedures must designate major decision points and start NEPA early
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall designate the major decision points for programs and actions subject to NEPA, ensuring the NEPA process begins at the earliest reasonable time and aligns with corresponding decision points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require that relevant environmental documents, comments, and responses be part of administrative records
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall require that relevant environmental documents, comments, and responses be part of the record in rulemaking and adjudicatory proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate environmental review into agency decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall integrate environmental review into the decision-making process by requiring that relevant environmental documents, comments, and responses accompany the proposal through existing agency review processes so decisionmakers use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another decision document accompanies environmental documents, agencies are encouraged to make available to the public any part relating to comparison of alternatives before the decision is made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require decisionmakers consider alternatives encompassed in environmental documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall require that the alternatives considered by the decisionmaker are encompassed by the range of alternatives discussed in relevant environmental documents and that the decisionmaker consider the alternatives described therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require combining environmental documents with other agency documents where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall require combination of environmental documents with other agency documents to facilitate sound and efficient decisionmaking and avoid duplication, consistent with statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include assistance to applicants in agency procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall include the assistance to applicants required by §1501.2(b)(4) (assistance to applicants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify typical classes of action requiring EISs or EAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall include specific criteria for and identification of those typical classes of action that normally (i) require environmental impact statements and (ii) require environmental assessments but not necessarily EISs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish categorical exclusions and identify extraordinary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing new or revising existing categorical exclusions, agencies shall: (i) identify when documentation of a determination that a categorical exclusion applies is required; (ii) substantiate proposed new/revised categorical exclusions with sufficient information to conclude the category does not have significant effects (individually or cumulatively) and provide this substantiation in a written record made publicly available as part of notice-and-comment; and (iii) describe how the agency will consider extraordinary circumstances consistent with §1501.4(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency procedures must include a process for reviewing categorical exclusions at least every 10 years (may be rolling) and describe identification of extraordinary circumstances that require further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for reviewing categorical exclusions at least every 10 years
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall include a process for reviewing the agency's categorical exclusions at least every 10 years, which the agency may conduct on a rolling basis starting with its oldest categorical exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processes for reevaluating and supplementing EAs and EISs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall include processes for reevaluating and supplementing environmental assessments and environmental impact statements, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public access to information and status of NEPA documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures shall explain where interested persons can get information or status reports on EISs, EAs, and other NEPA process elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures allowing applicant-prepared documents under agency supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an agency has applicants that seek its action, agency procedures shall allow an applicant (including an applicant-directed contractor) to prepare EAs and EISs under agency supervision, except when applicants serve as joint lead agencies; such procedures must be consistent with §1506.5 and at a minimum include:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Requirements for the agency to review and approve the purpose and need and reasonable alternatives; (ii) A process for the agency to independently evaluate the applicant-prepared EA or EIS, take responsibility for its accuracy, scope, and contents, and document the agency's evaluation in the document; and (iii) A prohibition on the preparation of a finding of no significant impact (FONSI) or record of decision (ROD) by applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional procedural inclusions agencies may adopt
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency procedures also may: (1) identify activities or decisions not subject to NEPA; (2) include processes for emergency actions that would not result in significant effects; (3) include criteria for limited exceptions for classified proposals and safeguard classified portions appropriately; and (4) provide for periods of time other than those in §1506.10 when necessary to comply with other statutory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified proposals properly classified may have environmental assessments/EISs with classified annexes so unclassified portions can be made public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency NEPA program information and public access via websites/IT tools
rubrics_metrics.description: To allow agencies and the public to efficiently access NEPA review information, agencies shall provide for agency websites or other IT tools to make available documents, relevant notices, and other relevant information for use by agencies, applicants, and interested persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Websites or other means shall include the agency's NEPA procedures (including subunits), and a list of environmental assessments and EISs in development and complete. As appropriate, agencies also should include agency planning documents guiding public involvement, environmental documents, policy documents, planning program information and tools, and a database searchable by geographic information, document status, document type, and project type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination of NEPA information technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall provide for efficient and effective interagency coordination of their environmental program websites and other IT tools, such as use of shared databases or APIs, in their implementation of NEPA and related authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Effects/Impacts (direct, indirect, cumulative) and scope of effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects or impacts mean changes to the human environment from the proposed action or alternatives that are reasonably foreseeable and include: (1) direct effects caused by the action occurring at the same time and place; (2) indirect effects caused later or farther removed but still reasonably foreseeable (may include growth-inducing effects); and (3) cumulative effects resulting from incremental effects when added to other past, present, and reasonably foreseeable actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects include ecological (natural resources, ecosystem components/structures/functioning), aesthetic, historic, cultural, economic, social, or health (including disproportionate and adverse effects on communities with environmental justice concerns), whether direct, indirect, or cumulative. Effects also include effects on Tribal resources and climate change-related effects, including contribution of a proposed action and reasonably foreseeable effects of climate change on the proposed action and alternatives. Effects may include both beneficial and adverse effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Environmental Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental justice means the just treatment and meaningful involvement of all people, regardless of income, race, color, national origin, Tribal affiliation, or disability, in agency decisionmaking and other Federal activities that affect human health and the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Environmental justice entails (1) full protection from disproportionate and adverse human health and environmental effects (including risks, climate-related impacts, cumulative impacts, and legacies of racism or structural barriers); and (2) equitable access to a healthy, sustainable, and resilient environment to live, play, work, learn, grow, worship, and engage in cultural and subsistence practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Categorical Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorical exclusion means a category of actions that an agency has determined, in its NEPA procedures or pursuant to §1501.4(c), normally does not have a significant effect on the human environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adopting or establishing categorical exclusions, agencies must still identify extraordinary circumstances that could make a normally excluded action significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Environmental Assessment (EA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental assessment means a concise public document, for which a Federal agency is responsible, for an action that is not likely to have a significant effect or for which the significance is unknown, used to support an agency's determination of whether to prepare an EIS or a finding of no significant impact (FONSI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Environmental Impact Statement (EIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental impact statement means a detailed written statement that is required by section 102(2)(C) of NEPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Environmental Document and Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental document means an EA, EIS, documented categorical exclusion determination, FONSI, record of decision, or notice of intent. Finding of no significant impact means a document briefly presenting the agency's determination and reasons why an action (not otherwise categorically excluded) will not have a significant effect and therefore an EIS will not be prepared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Extraordinary Circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Extraordinary circumstances are factors indicating that a normally categorically excluded action may have a significant effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include potential substantial effects on sensitive environmental resources; substantial disproportionate and adverse effects on communities with environmental justice concerns; substantial effects associated with climate change; and substantial effects on historic properties or cultural resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Human Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Human environment or environment means comprehensively the natural and physical environment and the relationship of present and future generations with that environment.
